lab_results.domain: clinical trial central laboratory results (long format, one test per row)

errors.kind: typo: extra zero / lost decimal point
errors.proof: Potassium 44.0 mmol/L is incompatible with life (reference 3.5-5.1, every other potassium in the file is 3-6); it is 4.4 with the decimal point lost, 10x the subject's other potassium results.

errors.kind: logical contradiction: result before collection
errors.proof: Result Date is 4 days before Collection Date; a sample cannot be resulted before it is drawn, and the same collection's other tests are resulted on or after the collection date.

traps.why: Potassium 6.8 mmol/L is a real critical hyperkalaemia, correctly flagged H; critical lab values occur in trials and must be reported, not corrected.
Hemoglobin 6.1 g/dL is severe anaemia, a real critical value flagged L, far below the others but physiologically possible.
Base excess is a signed quantity; -9.4 mmol/L is a real metabolic acidosis, flagged L. Negative values are normal in this test.
CRP 212 mg/L is a real acute infection/inflammation value (CRP routinely reaches 100-300+), flagged H; not a typo.

errors.kind: logical contradiction: entry debits do not equal credits (transposed digits)
errors.proof: Entry JE-1068: debit to Accounts Receivable equals revenue + 20% VAT for the original revenue 7647.67; the Sales Revenue credit reads 6747.67, so the entry's debits differ from its credits by 900.00 (digits transposed). VAT is exactly 20% of 7647.67.

errors.kind: broken formula: value typed over the Net formula
errors.proof: Every other Net cell is =Debit-Credit; this one is a typed constant 4540.79 that does not equal Debit 4127.99 minus Credit 0.

errors.kind: circular reference
errors.proof: The Net formula refers to its own cell (=RC), so Excel shows 0 while Credit is non-zero; every other Net is =Debit-Credit.

errors.kind: broken formula: points at the row above
errors.proof: This Net formula is =R[-1]C[-2]-R[-1]C[-1]: it shows the previous line's Debit-Credit instead of its own line's.

errors.kind: misspelt category
errors.proof: Account 2000 is named 'Accounts Payable' on every other line; this line reads 'Acounts Payable'.

errors.kind: domain rule: lines of one journal entry carry different posting dates
errors.proof: Entry JE-1080's lines 1 and 2 are posted 2026-03-16; line 3 is posted 2026-03-02. A journal entry posts on one date, so this line is mis-dated (it would fall into another period's balance).

traps.why: Storno (red) reversal: the accrual of JE posted 2026-01-30 is reversed with a negative debit; its entry still balances (-18,400 debit = -18,400 credit).
Negative credit on the storno reversal line, matching the negative debit of the same entry; valid reversal practice.
A real capital purchase of 486,500 debited to Equipment, balanced by Accounts Payable; far larger than routine lines but correct.

shipments.domain: multi-currency freight shipments with conversion to EUR

errors.kind: unit mismatch: grams in a kilogram column
errors.proof: A single courier piece of 1700.0 kg is impossible (courier pieces here are 0.3-30 kg, parcel limits ~70 kg), and its freight equals the courier rate for 1.7 kg: the weight was entered in grams.

errors.kind: logical contradiction: delivered before shipped
errors.proof: Delivery Date is 3 days before Ship Date, so Transit Days is -3; a shipment cannot arrive before it leaves.

errors.kind: broken formula: value typed over Freight EUR
errors.proof: Every other Freight EUR cell is =Freight Amount x FX Rate; this one is a typed constant (the previous row's Freight EUR) that does not equal its own amount x rate.

errors.kind: broken formula: points at the row above
errors.proof: Freight EUR here is =R[-1]C[-2]*R[-1]C[-1], the previous shipment's amount x rate, not its own.

errors.kind: unit mismatch: cents among dollars
errors.proof: USD 538621.0 for 1618.9 kg by air is about 100x the per-kg price of every other USD air shipment (3-4 EUR/kg + ~85 base); the amount was entered in cents (5386.21 USD).

errors.kind: misspelt category
errors.proof: Mode reads 'Courrier'; the column's modes are Air, Sea, Road and Courier.

traps.why: Amount 256742 is in JPY; yen amounts are ~150x EUR amounts, and Freight EUR converts it to a normal sea rate.
A courier document envelope of 0.3 kg; tiny next to pallets and containers but normal for Courier, priced at the courier minimum.
Same-day courier delivery within Europe: Transit Days 0 is valid (delivery equals ship date), not a missing value.

bom.domain: multi-level engineering bill of materials with extended quantities

errors.kind: circular reference
errors.proof: Extended Qty formula refers to its own cell (=RC), shows 0 although Qty Per and the parent's Extended Qty are non-zero; all other child lines use Qty Per x parent Extended Qty x (1+Scrap).

errors.kind: broken formula: value typed over Extended Qty
errors.proof: This child line's Extended Qty is a typed constant equal to Qty Per x parent qty without the parent's own multiplier (stale), not the column's formula Qty Per x parent Extended Qty x (1+Scrap).

errors.kind: broken formula: points at the wrong parent row
errors.proof: Its formula multiplies by the Extended Qty of the row just above its parent instead of its parent (named in Parent Part), unlike every sibling line.

errors.kind: unit mismatch: millimetres in a metre column
errors.proof: Qty Per 840 with UoM M means 840 metres of cable for one subassembly; every other M line is 0.5-3.0 m. It was entered in millimetres (0.84 m).

errors.kind: sign flip where the domain forbids negatives
errors.proof: A purchased hex bolt HB-M8X25 cannot be a by-product; the same part number is a positive quantity on every other line, so the negative Qty Per (and negative Extended Qty) is a sign error.

errors.kind: domain rule: child level is not its parent's level + 1
errors.proof: Level 3 but its Parent Part FX-9-SA4 is a level 1 subassembly; a child sits exactly one level below its parent (its siblings are level 2).

traps.why: A reference document line (assembly drawing) carries quantity 0 by design, so its Extended Qty is 0.
A negative component quantity is how ERP BOMs model a by-product (steel offcut returned to stock); its Extended Qty is legitimately negative.
30% scrap is normal for die-cut gaskets nested from sheet (the skeleton is waste), though far above the 1-8% of other lines.
